Reviewed on its merits per the orchestrator's instruction (not converged): the 2026-08-28 sequencing correction to AC-059/B6 (design.md:2783-2795, security-spec.md B6 row, acceptance-tests.md AC-059/TEST-059) is a security-boundary check (a 'high-risk design claim'; approval-surface write-scope) whose repair rests on a verification-path claim that design.md's own text does not support. The correction states T-007 registers TEST-059's grep and 'the registered check — a per-commit CI gate rather than a one-shot verification — covers the second family [`validate-resolver-evidence.*`] when T-008's commit lands,' analogized to how 'AC-032/AC-033/AC-034 bind every task's commits without per-task re-verification.' But design.md's own '## Deployment / CI Plan' (lines 2909-2917) states the opposite about CI-gating mechanics for this package: 'resolve-project-context.{py,sh,ps1}'s own CI registration (once implemented) is staged under specs/.../human-copy/ ... this Phase 1 package does not itself perform any CI wiring, only records the future task's own staging discipline,' and Test Strategy (lines 2172-2178) confirms every new suite is registered directly in the *unprotected* `tests/run-all.sh`/`.ps1`, while actual GitHub-Actions CI-gating requires a *separately staged, human-applied* `.github/workflows/test.yml` patch (matching AC-026/TEST-026's own explicit caveat: 'Status resolves through a human cp action for the test.yml portion'). Registering TEST-059's grep in run-all.sh at T-007's gate therefore makes it *invocable*, not automatically *per-commit CI-gated*, until that separate human action occurs — and nothing in the corrected text, in design.md's Deployment/CI Plan, or in the cited AC-032/033/034 analogy (which are themselves 'run once per task landing' procedural checks, not GitHub-Actions push-triggered gates) establishes that the human test.yml patch will have been applied, or that T-008's own Done-When requires a full `tests/run-all.sh` execution, by the time T-008 authors `validate-resolver-evidence.*`. This differs materially from AC-025's own case: AC-025's owner T-009 is downstream of every scanned script (investigation.md 'Ruling E's own repair'), so T-009 can verify the whole glob by direct execution at its own gate without depending on any future CI trigger; AC-059's repair, by contrast, is structurally dependent on a later, unscheduled event (T-008's commit reaching an already-CI-wired pipeline) to close the very gap the correction exists to close. Until design.md or the task package states that (a) the `test.yml` human-copy patch precedes T-008's landing, or (b) T-008's own Done-When independently runs the full suite including TEST-059's grep, the 'per-commit CI gate' verification path named for this security boundary is not concrete.
